title: When drug development gets personal
summary: When Third Rock Ventures partner Jigar Raythatha was diagnosed with brain cancer, he found himself relying on a drug originally developed by Agios, a biotech his firm backed years before he joined. On "The Top Line," he shares how the experience changed his perspective on drug development.

title: Chutes & Ladders—Lilly unifies global markets as 36-year vet Patrik Jonsson retires
summary: Lilly will unite its U.S. and international commercial units as a long-time exec retires. Enanta's CEO will hang up his hat after 23 year at the helm. Estrella has tapped a new a CEO to lead it through a clinical trial.

title: Bracco invests $230M in first US diagnostic imaging manufacturing facility
summary: Bracco announced it will invest $230 million to establish its first U.S. manufacturing facility for injectable contrast media in Sanford, North Carolina.

title: Jazz's $820M Actio buyout gives rise to Setara, armed with $90M series A
summary: Setara Biosciences, a privately held spinout formed following Jazz Pharmaceuticals' acquisition of Actio Biosciences in September, has raised $90 million in series A financing to advance its clinical-stage neuroscience drug candidate and earlier-stage pipeline.

title: AstraZeneca cuts early-phase prostate cancer pipeline
summary: AstraZeneca has punted a pair of early-phase prostate cancer programs as part of its quarterly pipeline clear out.

title: Bambusa shoots past IPO targets as Aspen trims offering
summary: Bambusa Therapeutics has upsized its IPO, selling more shares at the midpoint of its target range to gross $168.9 million for bispecific R&D. But Aspen Neuroscience underperformed expectations, hitting the bottom end of its target range and selling slightly fewer shares than expected.

title: Roche launches differential diagnosis test for mesothelioma
summary: Roche announced the global launch of its VENTANA BAP1 (SP527) test, an automated, ready-to-use immunohistochemistry (IHC) assay.

title: Sanofi considering ‘moonshot’ treatments as M&A targets to survive Dupixent patent cliff
summary: Sanofi is considering “moonshot” treatments among the potential acquisition targets needed for the French pharma to urgently replenish its pipeline, Chief Financial Officer François-Xavier Roger told Fierce.

title: Molecular Partners to lay off up to 44% of workforce in radiotherapy pivot
summary: Molecular Partners plans to lay off up to 44% of its staff as it focuses its declining cash reserves on a radiotherapeutic pipeline led by an early-phase small cell lung cancer drug candidate.

title: Eli Lilly scraps phase 2 Alzheimer's program after drug falls short of expectations
summary: Eli Lilly has dropped its phase 2 Alzheimer's disease program for mevidalen, marking another setback for the experimental drug as the Big Pharma expands its neuroscience pipeline through multibillion-dollar acquisitions.

title: Merck outlines 2027 as ‘another year of investment’ despite recent clinical wins
summary: Even as a wave of clinical trial wins bolsters its momentum, Merck & Co. is prioritizing ongoing pipeline and commercial expansions over near-term margin growth, hoping to strengthen its long-term prospects past Keytruda's loss of exclusivity.

title: BMS walks away from $80M neurodegeneration bet after phase 1
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb has scrapped a phase 1 program it bet $80 million on just two years ago.

title: BioMarin inks up to $475M deal to challenge Fabry ERT incumbents
summary: BioMarin is paying $70 million upfront to license a Fabry disease drug candidate, expanding the franchise it acquired through its $4.8 billion takeover of Amicus Therapeutics.

title: Flagship brings 3 biotech platforms together to launch AI drug discovery player Etcelera
summary: Flagship Pioneering unveiled Etcelera today, a new AI-powered biotech emerging from stealth that aims to predict how potential medicines will act in patients.

title: Geron’s Rytelo stumbles in phase 3 as Novartis gears up for post-JAK inhibitor blood cancer bid
summary: Geron has discontinued a phase 3 trial of its Rytelo in JAK inhibitor-pretreated myelofibrosis after an independent data monitoring committee ruled that the study was unlikely to succeed, just as Novartis is gearing up for a delayed FDA approval bid for its pelabresib.

title: Oura, UC San Diego Health collaborate to study GLP-1 outcomes using continuous smart ring data
summary: Oura is pushing further into clinical healthcare research with its first clinical trial to study the link between smart ring data and obesity-treatment outcomes.

title: Ascletis’ challenger to Lilly’s Foundayo hits goals in phase 2 diabetes trial
summary: A phase 2 trial of Ascletis’ oral GLP-1 drug candidate has hit its primary and secondary endpoints, positioning the Chinese biotech to mount a two-front attack on Eli Lilly’s Foundayo.

title: Genmab's $8B Merus bet delivers as bispecific combo halves risk of death in phase 3
summary: Capping off a busy few days in Spain, Genmab reported results from the first interim analysis of a phase 3 trial showing that adding its bispecific antibody petosemtamab to Merck & Co.'s Keytruda cut the risk of death by 50% compared with Keytruda alone in patients with PD-L1-positive recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

title: FDA’s rare disease framework aims to ‘stand the test of time’
summary: During a public hearing Wednesday to discuss a newly proposed rare disease framework, FDA center director Michael Davis, M.D., Ph.D., said the agency aims to design a scheme that “stands the test of time.”

title: Biogen CEO tells analysts he’s focused on early-stage R&D as ‘we were not very good with that’
summary: Biogen's CEO has pointed to the company's ability to take five drugs into clinical trials so far this year as evidence of its new focus on early-stage R&D.

title: ‘The patient need is enormous’: Syntax programs stem cells into pancreatic beta cells in 4 days
summary: Chicago-based Syntax Bio believes it has cracked the code for turning stem cells into pancreatic beta cells in as little as four days.

title: Lilly’s retatrutide bests Ozempic on blood sugar, weight loss in phase 3 diabetes showdown
summary: Eli Lilly’s triple-G drug candidate retatrutide has beaten Novo’s Ozempic in a head-to-head phase 3 trial, driving deeper reductions in blood sugar and body weight across the 80-week study.

title: GSK predicts ‘some limited impact’ to UK roles as restructuring rolls on
summary: GSK’s global restructuring plan is likely to see “some limited impact” to roles on the Big Pharma’s home turf of the U.K., executives have confirmed.

title: How Your Brain Saves Nostalgia From Scandals
summary: Can you separate the art from the artist? A new study shows our brains do it automatically: when a beloved creator falls from grace, memory performs "moral surgery," downgrading the person while protecting nostalgic memories of their art.

title: How to Map Brain Circuits Without Touching a Single Neuron
summary: How can scientists determine cause and effect when experiments are impossible? summary: Why do some hugs stay with us while others fade away? A survey of more than 15,000 UK adults published in PLOS One shows that 70% remember hugs for comfort, with empathy, relationship attachment styles, and body perception dictating how touch is stored in memory.

title: Serotonin signaling enhances phagocytosis by brain macrophages through Htr2b and alleviates brain injury after stroke
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02482-yThe serotonin receptor Htr2b activation enhances lysosome biogenesis and phagocytic clearance of debris to mitigate neuroinflammation and brain injury after stroke. The study proposes a potential monocyte-derived macrophage-targeted immune therapy to improve neurological outcomes after ischemic stroke.

title: Stimulus-specific recruitment of human amygdala neurons predicts episodic memory encoding success
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02493-9The study shows that stimulus-specific neurons in the human amygdala determine which experiences become lasting memory, revealing a mechanism that predicts episodic memory formation and may guide future treatments for memory disorders.

title: Circuit mechanisms for disentangled representations and generalization in the hippocampus
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02491-xThe hippocampus encodes different aspects of experience as disentangled variables, enabling flexible recombination and generalization to new situations. This code is supported by the geometry of population dynamics and cell–assembly interactions.

title: Chronic progressive demyelination induces a microglial state with lysosomal dysfunction
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02489-5Acute myelin injury responses are well defined, but microglia adaptations to chronic damage remain unclear. Mouse models reveal a chronic demyelination-associated microglial state marked by inflammation, lysosomal dysfunction and myelin-damaging activity.

title: Microglial NUS1 deficiency drives dopaminergic neurodegeneration through intercellular iron dysregulation in Parkinson’s disease models
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02499-3Using cellular and mouse models, this study reports that deficiency of the Parkinson’s disease risk gene NUS1 in microglia disrupts intercellular iron homeostasis, leading to neuronal iron overload and dopaminergic neurodegeneration.
